articles.title: Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become UN secretary general
articles.excerpt: Michelle Bachelet, a former president of Chile, has withdrawn her candidacy to become the next secretary general of the ⁠UN, ending an attempt ​that had struggled to gain traction among security council members.Bachelet, 74, announced ⁠her decision in a video posted on Instagram on Saturday, saying: “I will now continue, with the ⁠same determination as always, my international work.”The two-time Chilean ​president and former ‌UN human ‌rights chief had positioned her campaign around defending multilateralism and ‌international law at a time when she said both were under sustained pressure.Bachelet’s exit leaves seven candidates in the race to succeed António Guterres, who will conclude his second five-year term as secretary general on ‌31 December. It is still possible for more candidates to enter the contest.Her ​withdrawal comes after a third informal straw poll, held on Friday, showed her support had all but collapsed. That same poll put Costa ⁠Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan in the lead.The UN security ​council ​will formally recommend ​a single candidate to the 193-member general ​assembly for election. ‌The assembly’s ​approval ​has long been seen as a formality once the council reaches consensus.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election
articles.excerpt: Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the presidential election.On 4 October, the leftwing incumbent will face the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who has been gaining ground in recent weeks.The rise in the monthly payment, from about £98 to £113, that he announced on Thursday is due to take effect on 19 October, just before the likely runoff vote on 25 October.The increase is expected to benefit between 15% and 20% of voters in what promises to be one of the closest ever presidential races in Latin America’s largest country.Lula said it was not really an increase, but an adjustment in line with inflation to “protect the purchasing power of the most vulnerable families”, but his opponents have criticised its timing so close to the election.Flávio Bolsonaro called it an “act of desperation” after polls showed him gaining ground – although the most recent survey, released on Thursday night, still showed Lula numerically ahead despite the technical tie.

articles.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
articles.excerpt: A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.Researchers used genetic data to confirm that the cat is a new species, and gave it the scientific name Leopardus tilcayo, retaining its local name.A Leopardus tilcayo cat at the Senda Verde animal refuge in the Yungas region of Bolivia on 1 September 2026. Photograph: Fernando Faciole/National Geographic/Reuters“Its fur is light brown … with irregularly shaped rosettes across its body,” said Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a National Geographic explorer and one of the authors ⁠of the study describing the newly identified species published on Thursday in the journal Current Biology.Little is yet known about the cat’s biology and lifestyle. Remains of small rodents in scat ​samples suggest they may form part of its diet, while camera-trap evidence indicates it ‌could be more active at night, Nogales-Ascarrunz said.Tiger ‌cats are so-called cryptic species, meaning they cannot easily be distinguished merely by appearance, said evolutionary biologist and study co-lead author Jonas Lescroart of the University of Antwerp in Belgium.Tiger ‌cats previously had been considered a single species, but genetic studies decades ago suggested the existence of multiple species.A tilcayo cat, the only known individual of the newly identified species living in protective captivity.

articles.title: All smiles in Strasbourg but uncertainty clouds Canada’s EU membership plan
articles.excerpt: Mark Carney received a rapturous reception in the European parliament when he gave his speech on Thursday welcoming a proposal for Canada to become the EU’s first-ever associate member.Politicians queued to shake his hand and take selfies. One described the speech as a historic moment. “Europe has extended a hand, and Canada has taken it,” said the German Green MEP Terry Reintke, who borrowed a Canadian ice hockey shirt for the occasion.One day earlier, in the same debating chamber, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, issued the unprecedented invitation to Canada – an idea quickly derided by Donald Trump, who threatened Europe with “heavy tariffs” if it became a reality.But the prospect of Canada’s associate membership is uncertain, not least because no one is sure what it means. “I’m not quite sure why she [von der Leyen] used that term because there’s simply no legal definition,” said one senior politician. “This has just raised lots of questions. So people are talking more about what an associate membership means instead of … this unique partnership and alliance for the future that EU-Canada relations should be about.”The German chancellor Friedrich Merz’s spokesperson welcomed the initiative for a close partnership with Canada and said Germany was “open to discussing new models that reflect the special significance of the relationship”, but called for the associate membership label to be “reconsidered”.Trump calls EU’s offer of associate membership to Canada ‘laughable’ – videoMerz himself has floated “associate membership” for Ukraine, as a stepping stone to joining the bloc, but this was quickly dismissed by other member states.One EU diplomat said von der Leyen “seemed a bit far out in floating this” and that even before Wednesday’s speech member states had worried that she was overpromising on Canada.

articles.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development
articles.excerpt: About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.In response, he started developing his own AI study tool, concluding: “If you can’t beat them, join them.”The pace and quality of AI development in China is second only to the United States, with the two superpowers locked in an intensifying rivalry as the stakes rise with each new model’s capabilities.Analysts generally agree that frontier, or cutting-edge, US models are still some way ahead of their Chinese counterparts.But over the last few weeks the mood music from Silicon Valley has been decidedly sombre, as insider after insider has warned of the potential catastrophes that could result from “loss of control” of the most advanced AIs.And last Saturday Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei pitched a “worldwide pacing of the frontier” – something he said would “require cooperation with China”.“China is definitely not receptive” to a slowdown on US firms’ terms, though, said Lian Jye Su from technology research group Omdia.For the government, AI is a “core sovereignty capability”, and Beijing will not want to jeopardise the progress made in closing the gap with US frontier models.“It sees these calls [for a slowdown] as a bid to lock in US advantage,” said Su.Amodei made this explicit, mentioning China specifically when arguing it was key “to keep democracies’ AI lead over autocracies as large as possible”.He advocated for measures including continued export controls to China on advanced chips and machinery – the existence of which some argue already amounts to a forced unilateral “pacing”.China’s foreign ministry responded to Amodei’s piece by saying “fearmongering,

articles.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty
articles.excerpt: An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.Police said she died of suffocation.Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya provincial court, where he pleaded not guilty to all charges, a court spokesperson said.He had been charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor for indecent purposes. The next court date was set for 12 October.Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl in the early hours of 25 June, and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.In a police interrogation video shared online by Thai media, Carman has said he was acting in self-defence because the girl was threatening him with a knife.The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.

articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
articles.excerpt: Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.Wednesday’s La Liga fixture between Levante and Athletic Club had to be postponed due to flooding at the Estadio Ciudad de Valencia. On Thursday rescuers found the body of a man near Olivella, west of Barcelona, after his car was swept away in the waters. Spain’s east coast is susceptible to extreme rainfall during the autumn months, as experienced in 2024, when devastating flash floods killed more than 200 people in Valencia. With the Mediterranean Sea reaching record temperatures, this is providing extra fuel and moisture to thunderstorms, making flooding more likely.In New Jersey in the US on Sunday, the Racefaster half marathon was disrupted due to extreme rainfall and a partly submerged course. Runners had to wade through chest-deep waters at times as 50mm-100mm of rain fell. Despite the flooding, 250 people managed to finish the race. Flooding was also reported to the north-east in Connecticut and Rhode Island, where up to 190mm of rain was recorded in a 36-hour period.Tropical Storm Dujuan, currently over the open west Pacific Ocean, will move north-west on a track towards Japan over the coming days. It is forecast to intensify into a category one typhoon on Friday.

articles.title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices
articles.excerpt: Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran.The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.The move meant the BoJ joined the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in tightening monetary policy this month, as central banks attempt to curb the impact of rising prices, linked to the conflict in the Middle East.The Bank of England on Thursday voted to leave UK interest rates on hold at 3.75% but warned they could soon rise amid the fallout from the Iran war.The BoJ policy committee’s vote to raise rates was not unanimous – with two of the nine board members dissenting against the increase.Kazuo Ueda, the governor of the BoJ, would not rule out the possibility of back-to-back rate rises by the bank’s policy committee.“That depends on how price conditions develop,” he said. “There could be various possibilities. We shouldn’t rule anything out. We’re at a phase where we need to look at various data carefully. But that doesn’t mean we can move slowly. We will analyse data carefully and take timely action as needed.”The BoJ’s policy committee meets eight times a year, roughly once every six weeks, and Ueda said there is no set plan for the timing of any future potential increases in the rate.“As for the pace of future rate hikes, we don’t have any pre-set idea in mind such as once every three months,” he said. “We will determine at each policy meeting how best to ensure underlying inflation stabilises ‌at 2%.”Ueda said the BoJ has changed its policy of trying to boost inflation in the economy to focusing on ensuring it does not go above its target of 2%. In August the rate of inflation in Japan was 1.9%.“Up until ​now, our short-term ‌policy focus was ​to push ​up underlying inflation from levels below 2%,” he said. “Now, underlying inflation is approaching 2%.

articles.title: South Korea will not send military to support US war on Iran, defying Trump pressure
articles.excerpt: South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, has said he will ⁠not deploy the military to the ⁠Middle East in a way ​that could draw the country into conflict, resisting calls from Donald Trump to support his war in Iran.“There won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war. I can tell you that very clearly,” Lee said at a ⁠news conference on Friday. “We won’t deploy military assets in any form to that end.”However, Lee added that he was reviewing whether to play a greater role in safeguarding navigation in the region.

articles.title: Australia news live: Taylor says fuel price policy would be funded by tobacco excise cut; Albanese to put AI concerns to Trump
articles.excerpt: From 1h agoCoalition plans to use cut in tobacco excise to fund fuel tax policyAngus Taylor says the Coalition would cut the tobacco excise to fund halving the fuel excise, despite health experts sounding the alarm about the move. Speaking on Nine’s Today, the opposition leader said his party’s policy to slash the fuel excise in half when global prices hit US$100 over two weeks “won’t put pressure on inflation, despite what the treasurer is trying to say, he has it wrong”. When asked about previous criticisms from health experts about slashing the tobacco excise and what it would mean for anti-smoking efforts, Taylor said: double quotation markI think the health experts need to explain why they’re OK with … organised crime in this country, criminal gangs in this country, controlling the tobacco trade. 80% of the trade is illegal. You can already buy a packet of cigarettes for 15 bucks a pack or less. So I mean, seriously, we can’t take those comments seriously. Key events1h agoCoalition plans to use cut in tobacco excise to fund fuel tax policy3h agoAlbanese says he will put concerns about AI to Trump3h agoJim Chalmers to release intergenerational report with AI warnings3h agoAlbanese launches bid for Australia for two-year seat on UN security council3h agoFormer NSW police officer’s double murder trial to get under way3h agoFormer top aide to Lachlan Murdoch gets senior diplomatic post in NYNSW police detail ‘horrific’ scenes after Blue Mountains stabbingsPeter McKenna, deputy commissioner for NSW police, just spoke after an alleged stabbing attack by a mother against her three young children, which left one child dead and two others in critical condition.McKenna said the mother, aged in her 40s, is also in critical condition after the incident, which took place in the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney, on Sunday afternoon.
articles.summary: 1小时前：联盟党计划通过削减烟草税来为燃油税政策提供资金。安格斯·泰勒表示，联盟党将削减烟草消费税，以资助将燃油消费税减半的计划，尽管卫生专家对该举措发出警告。这位反对党领袖在九号电视台的《今日秀》节目中表示，他的政党提出的在全球油价连续两周达到每桶100美元时将燃油消费税减半的政策，「不会给通胀带来压力，不管财长想怎么说，他说错了」。当被问及卫生专家此前对削减烟草税的批评以及这对反吸烟努力意味着什么时，泰勒表示：「我认为卫生专家需要解释，为什么他们对……这个国家的有组织犯罪、这个国家的犯罪团伙控制烟草交易无动于衷。80%的交易是非法的。你现在已经可以以每包15澳元甚至更低的价格买到一包香烟。所以，我是说，说真的，我们不能把这些评论当回事。」关键事件：1小时前，联盟党计划通过削减烟草税为燃油税政策提供资金；3小时前，阿尔巴尼斯表示他将向特朗普提出对AI的担忧；3小时前，吉姆·查默斯将发布带有AI警告的代际报告；3小时前，阿尔巴尼斯发起澳大利亚竞选联合国安理会两年期席位的努力；3小时前，前新南威尔士州警官双重谋杀案庭审即将开始；3小时前，拉克兰·默多克的前高级助手获得纽约高级外交职位。新州警方详述蓝山刺伤事件后的「骇人」场面。新南威尔士州警方副局长彼得·麦肯纳刚刚就一名母亲涉嫌刺伤其三幼童、导致一名儿童死亡、另外两人伤势危急的事件发表讲话。麦肯纳表示，这名40多岁的母亲在事件发生后也处于危急状态，事件于周日下午发生在悉尼以西的蓝山地区。

articles.title: Police allege mother behind Blue Mountains stabbing attack on three children that left one dead
articles.excerpt: Police have alleged that a mother was behind a stabbing attack on three young children that left one dead and two others fighting for their lives in hospital.The woman, aged in her 40s, is also in a critical condition.Bystanders were first on the scene after finding the three children and the woman with stab wounds inside a vehicle at Valley Heights in the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney, on Sunday afternoon.One young child died at the scene despite witnesses rushing to help, delivering first aid while waiting for emergency services to arrive.The alleged domestic violence incident came at the end of a horror weekend across New South Wales, after three women were allegedly murdered inside their homes within a 12-hour period on Saturday.The police deputy commissioner Peter McKenna described the past two days as devastating.“It’s a horrific and tragic weekend and it’s like one that I don’t remember in my career,” he told Nine’s Today on Monday.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email“Those three … plus the no-more-tragic situation that we had in the Blue Mountains. Put them all together and it’s unfathomable.”Paramedics treated the mother and children at the scene on Sunday before taking them by road to Westmead hospital and Westmead Children’s hospital in a critical condition, where they remained.“The two children and their mother are in a critical condition,” McKenna said.“The mother is the suspect in this matter, for domestic related homicide, and that investigation is ongoing.”Hours after the incident, NSW police Supt John Nelson said the father of the children had been notified.The father had been at work when he received the call from police, he said.“You can imagine receiving that tragic news,” Nelson told reporters.He said the woman had not previously come to the attention of police and that investigators were not looking for anyone else in relation to the incident.The woman was aged in her 40s and the children were all under five.
articles.summary: 警方指控一名母亲是刺伤三名幼童、导致一人死亡、另外两人在医院与死神搏斗的袭击事件的幕后黑手。这名40多岁的女子也处于危急状态。周日下午，在悉尼以西蓝山地区的谷高地，旁观者发现三名儿童和这名女子在一辆车内身中刀伤，最先赶到现场。一名幼童当场死亡，尽管目击者急忙施救，在等待急救人员到达时进行了急救。这起涉嫌家庭暴力事件发生在新南威尔士州一个恐怖周末的尾声，此前周六在12小时内有三名女性涉嫌在家中被杀害。警察副局长彼得·麦肯纳将过去两天描述为毁灭性的。「这是一个骇人而悲惨的周末，是我职业生涯中不记得有过的，」他周一告诉九号电视台的《今日秀》。「那三起……再加上我们在蓝山遇到的最悲惨的情况。把它们加在一起，简直难以想象。」急救人员周日现场救治了母亲和孩子们，随后以危急状态通过公路将他们送往韦斯特米德医院和韦斯特米德儿童医院，他们仍留在那里。「两名儿童和他们的母亲处于危急状态，」麦肯纳说。「这名母亲是本案的嫌疑人，涉及家庭相关凶杀，调查正在进行中。」事件发生数小时后，新州警方警司约翰·纳尔逊表示，孩子们的父亲已被告知。他说，父亲接到警方电话时正在上班。「你可以想象接到那样悲惨的消息，」纳尔逊告诉记者。他说，这名女子此前未曾引起警方注意，调查人员也未在寻找与事件相关的其他任何人。这名女子40多岁，孩子们均不满五岁。

articles.title: Albanese launches bid for UN security council seat and names former Murdoch aide to top diplomatic post
articles.excerpt: Australia having a seat at the United Nations Security Council will be able to help with the cost of living back home, the prime minister insists.Anthony Albanese has launched a formal bid for Australia to serve a two-year term on the UN security council in 2029 and 2030.Albanese also unveiled former News Corp head of broadcasting Siobhan McKenna as Australia’s next consul general to New York.A vote for the UN council spot won’t be held until mid 2028, but lobbying efforts will intensify during the prime minister’s visit to New York for the UN general assembly.The prime minister said Australia’s role on the council would be able to benefit ordinary citizens.“Engagement with the world matters. It matters because it makes a difference to the cost of living, to inflation, to Australians’ way of life,” he told reporters in New York on Monday, Australian time.“That is why we can’t afford to not be engaged with the world, because it has a direct impact on the quality of life of Australians on a day-to-day basis.“We have an opportunity through this potential seat on the UN security council to play a key role in shaping the global issues that really matter to Australians.”Australia has served on the security council five times since the UN was established after the second world war.The most recent stint was in 2013 and 2014, where Australia was able to lead a response to the Russian downing of Malaysia Airlines flight MH17.Anthony Albanese unveiled former News Corp head of broadcasting Siobhan McKenna as Australia’s next consul general to New York. Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty ImagesAlbanese said the role Australia played during that period was evidence of what a spot on the council could achieve.“We do need to stand up to the Middle East conflict.

articles.title: One Nation-linked company built $56,000 shed on private property of Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man
articles.excerpt: Pauline Hanson’s right-hand man, James Ashby, is enjoying generous benefits as a result of his role working for One Nation, with documents showing that a company linked to the party built a $56,000 shed on his central Queensland property.Guardian Australia understands that Ashby, formerly Hanson’s chief of staff and now the party’s national director, also drives a new Ford Ranger that was “personally” gifted to One Nation by Hancock Agriculture’s chief executive, Adam Giles, in April. Hanson said the vehicle would help the party’s campaign efforts and “provides us the presence we need in the lead-up to the next federal election”.Sources say Ashby is earning a lucrative salary in his new high-profile role. He also has regular access to the $2m Cirrus plane gifted to the party by Giles’ employer and Australia’s richest person, Gina Rinehart.The aircraft is kept at Rockhampton airport, not far from Ashby’s home, and he is its main pilot.The Populist The Populist: The favourite son | Episode 2 – podcastSorry your browser does not support audio - but you can download here and listen $https://audio.guim.co.uk/2026/09/20-27700-THE_POPULIST_E2_FAVOURITE_SON.mp300:00:0001:04:45In a statement to Guardian Australia, Ashby said the car was used “for campaign and branch purposes” while the plane was “not used for personal transportation”.“I have a privately owned vehicle for personal use,” he said.A friend of Ashby’s travelled on the plane with him and Hanson on its maiden flight to Albury in May. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here Property records show that Ashby bought a “lifestyle property” near Yeppoon in Queensland in 2025.

articles.title: The gunzels’ grand final: Melbourne Tramaroos’ campaign derails at European TramDriver Championship
articles.excerpt: It’s the grand final for gunzels. But despite having one of the largest tram networks in the world, Melbourne’s Tramaroos finished second last at this year’s European TramDriver Championship, just ahead of London.The event, held in Warsaw on Saturday, saw 26 teams compete across a series of demanding tasks, inspired – to varying degrees – by tram drivers’ day-to-day work.In smooth stop and go, drivers travelled with a bowl of water attached to the front of the tram – with points deducted for every drop spilled. Other precision tasks involved speed control at 25 km/h, target braking, tram bowling, lateral distance, basketball, a perfect stop with the second door, and a reverse ride guided by whistle commands.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailDaniel Bowen, a spokesperson for the Public Transport Users Association, said it was “an unusual event in the pantheon of world sports”.“It’s pretty entertaining,” he said, and an opportunity to look for inspiration from other tram systems around the world. “Everyone looked like they were having a great time.”The basketball component. Photograph: Dawid Wolski/East News/ShutterstockThis year’s title went to Vendula Tmejová and Zdeněk Rychtář, from Prague, in the Czech Republic.In 2022, Australia was the first ever non-European country chosen to participate. This year, Yarra Trams sent Ivan Cavanagh of Southbank depot and Claudia Barrientos from Kew depot to compete as the “Tramaroos”. Had they won, the trophy would have gone “straight to the pool room”, Cavanagh said.“You would hope our team would do well but I’m sure there’s pretty stiff competition against you know the Europeans,” Bowen said. “Perhaps it’s a bit like Eurovision – it’s great to participate.”A member of the Danish team from Odense celebrates after their final run.

articles.title: Friedrich Merz vows to stay in office after CDU ‘disaster’ in German state elections
articles.excerpt: Germany’s embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, has vowed to stay in office and fight for future-proofing economic changes despite heavy losses for his conservatives in two state elections, one to the far right and the other to a leftwing party.Preliminary results indicated Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU) tallied just over the 5% threshold to enter the state parliament in the coastal region of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, its worst-ever state score, which he called a “disaster”.The anti-immigration, Kremlin-friendly Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party extended a streak of strong showings by coming in first in the former communist region with nearly 38%, more than doubling its previous score.In the capital, Berlin, one of Germany’s 16 federal states, the far-left Die Linke looked on course to win with about 25% of the vote, ahead of the incumbent CDU by a five-point margin. The AfD made headway there too, with a clear double-digit result.The deeply unpopular Merz has been fighting for his political survival after a humiliating series of setbacks with voters this year.Speculation about his ability to hold on as chancellor reached fever pitch after Saxony-Anhalt state’s AfD chapter routed the CDU with a record 44% for the party in an election two weeks ago.The Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania result marked the third time the AfD has emerged as the strongest party in a region, although the party seemed likely to remain shut out of power in the state because of a “firewall” of non-cooperation agreed by the other main parties.In a rare speech on a state election night, Merz admitted the CDU had been bitterly deprived of “tailwinds from Berlin” in both of Sunday’s races.

articles.title: Man, 82, dies after brawl with 76-year-old over sunlounger on Greek beach
articles.excerpt: Greek police are investigating the death of an 82-year-old man after a brawl over a sunlounger at a beach on the Athenian riviera.The man had arrived at the popular bathing spot of Vouliagmeni before 10am on Sunday hoping to secure a sunbed, but he soon began arguing with a fellow bather – described by authorities as a “76-year-old man unknown to him” – when it became clear loungers were in short supply.The row quickly degenerated into a scuffle as others reportedly joined in. The victim, who was with his wife, is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest during the fight.“It seems that people who were with [the assailant] also participated,” ERT, the country’s state broadcaster, reported.“The 82-year-old was seriously injured, and needed to be transferred by ambulance to Asklepieion hospital in Voula.“Despite the efforts of doctors, at about 11am the elderly man succumbed to his wounds.”A postmortem was immediately ordered.Police arrested the 76-year-old and, initially, a 21-year-old woman who was with him. The beach resort’s manager was also detained for questioning.“The incident is under investigation,” said a source, describing the fight as unprecedented. “In Greece disagreement is expressed vocally, with a lot of screaming and shouting, not in fistfights like this – especially between two elderly men. I think that’s why it is so shocking.”Like other parts of Europe, Greece is undergoing a severe cost of living crisis that has heightened tensions and put strain on social relations. An increase in domestic violence and other disputes has been partly blamed on the pressures of everyday life.In recent years, there has been growing anger over private rental outfits hogging prime coastal areas with exorbitantly priced sunloungers in Greece, where the sea has an important place in national identity.Authorities said “all those” involved in the incident would appear before a magistrate.

articles.title: European spy chiefs warn Moscow is planning more decisive action against Nato
articles.excerpt: European intelligence officials have raised the possibility of an imminent Russian test of Nato, with one saying a potential attack could come in a matter of “months, not years”.The warnings come after Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, told parliament that intelligence assessments suggested Russia might launch an attack with drones or missiles on Nato territory in the coming months, as part of efforts to prove that “article 5 is more theoretical than practical”.The French president, Emmanuel Macron, called Tusk’s warnings “sound and well-documented”, and on Friday summoned party leaders and 2027 presidential candidates for an emergency meeting in Paris, where they discussed – among other topics – intelligence of a growing threat from Russia.The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, alongside Adm Viktor Liina, the commander of Russia’s Pacific fleet. Photograph: Gavriil Grigorov/AFP/Getty ImagesThe escalation fears come as the UN general assembly convenes in New York later this week, and amid intensifying airstrikes on both sides of Russia’s war on Ukraine. Kyiv hit Moscow and other Russian regions with hundreds of drones and missiles in the early hours of Sunday, in one of its biggest air attacks of the war.In separate interviews with the Guardian over the past week, in different locations, three European intelligence leaders discussed their views of the potential threat from Moscow.Michal Koudelka, the head of the Czech Republic’s BIS security service, said that as well as increased drone activity, a small-scale invasion of Nato territory that bordered Russia could be part of the Kremlin’s plans. “It’s possible. It could involve a limited incursion, false-flag provocations, a massive influence campaign,” he said, in a rare interview at the agency’s headquarters in Prague.

articles.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with hundreds of drones on final day of Russian election
articles.excerpt: Ukraine has targeted Moscow and the surrounding region in a large-scale attack that involved hundreds of drones.The attack killed at least three people and damaged what Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said was one of Russia’s “key oil industry facilities” on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.Zelenskyy said that among the weapons used in the attack was the Pelican, initially thought to be a short-range ballistic missile, but which sources said later was a winged drone.Fires at Moscow oil refinery facility after drone attackThe president did not offer any further details, prompting media reports in Ukraine that it was a ballistic missile, only for doubt to be cast on the weapon identification later in the day.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine had used its domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles to strike Moscow. The long-range weapon has previously been used against targets deep inside Russia and has the range to reach the country’s capital.Ukrainian and Russian Telegram channels posted images of what they said was debris from a Flamingo missile found in the Moscow region, though the claims could not be independently verified. Ruslan Leviev, the head of the open-source investigation group Conflict Intelligence Team, said the debris probably came from a Flamingo missile.Workers at Fire Point’s secret factory in Ukraine inspect one of their FP-5 Flamingo missiles last year. Photograph: Efrem Lukatsky/APMoscow’s mayor, Sergey Sobyanin, said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow, though these figures are often exaggerated, and Ukraine’s daily drone fire rate estimated a number in the low hundreds.Sobyanin accused Ukraine of attempting to interfere with a tightly controlled three-day election in Russia that is expected to tighten Vladimir Putin’s 26-year grip on power.“The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections.

articles.title: ‘I have nothing in the UK at all’: British man torn from his Swedish wife and home
articles.excerpt: Doubled over a Heathrow baggage trolley, the former British business director is sobbing uncontrollably, exhausted emotionally and physically after being deported from Sweden.Hours earlier the 65-year-old had been marched on to a plane in Stockholm, separated from his home and his Swedish wife after a five-year battle to stay in the country after Brexit came to an end.An only child with no children and no property in the UK, Charles has in effect been made homeless. He was last in the UK in 2022 for one week, and before that not since 2017 when he emigrated.“I have nothing, nothing in the UK at all,” says Charles as he shows a text from the British consulate explaining where in Heathrow those suddenly left homeless can get help.“All I want is to return to my wife, my home and my friends in Sweden and to live a quiet, peaceful life,” adds Charles, who does not want to publicly share his full identity.His forced flight on Tuesday shows that deportations of British citizens who lived in Sweden before Brexit are continuing. Stockholm has already deported 458 British people after rejected residency applications, a higher proportion in terms of its population than any EU member state.Charles is distraught after landing at Heathrow. Photograph: David Levene/The GuardianThe situation persists despite promises from opposition parties now on track to form a government that they will introduce urgent laws to give Britons a second chance to apply for residency.“I’ve done nothing wrong but feel I’ve been treated like a criminal,” Charles says.“Since arriving in Sweden nearly nine years ago, I’ve done everything I can to integrate myself into Swedish society. I’ve learned some basic Swedish, contributed to Swedish society and the Swedish economy, and for that, I’m being punished.

articles.title: Middle East braces for more violence as Iran claims US is planning to renew bombing campaign
articles.excerpt: Governments across the Middle East are bracing for an escalation of violence after Iran claimed it had received intelligence that the US was preparing for a renewed bombing campaign against the Islamic Republic.In a potential sign of growing tensions before the UN general assembly in New York this week, Donald Trump cut short a weekend visit to the Camp David presidential retreat on Sunday with no official explanation, and a new security alert was issued by the state department to all US citizens in the Middle East.Keeping his options open, Trump reportedly told a Fox News reporter “very big things are going to be happening in the not-so-distant future” and that the options he was considering were “wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically or making a deal”.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned that if an attack does take place, “all US bases and interests in the region will become targets of continuous, effective and painful attacks without any limitations or considerations”.Map indicating territory under de facto Houthi authority as of 11 SeptemberIran’s leaders also pledged some of the reprisals could extend as far as US naval forces in the Indian Ocean, and accused some Gulf leaders of “double-dealing” by allegedly giving a green light to the US attacks.The outburst of sabre-rattling appears to have been prompted by attacks on the Saudi capital, Riyadh, by Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi rebels. The barrage on Saturday marked the first time the capital’s Aramco oil facilities had been subject to such a sustained attack since the Saudi-Houthi ceasefire broke down in June. Riyadh insisted it had intercepted the missiles, but local photographs show smoke pouring from the Aramco facility.

articles.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
articles.excerpt: Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday.The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July.Explosions were heard in Riyadh as firefighters battled to extinguish the flames of a burning fuel tank emblazoned with the logo of the Saudi oil company Aramco near the city’s King Khalid international airport.Map showing location of King Khalid airport in Saudi Arabia and wider regionResidents told Agence France-Presse that hours after the alert, they had heard what sounded like another round of explosions echoing through parts of the Saudi capital.According to tracking website FlightRadar24, there were “major problems” at the airport and it has been listed under its maximum disruption index.“In the direction of the airport, we saw black smoke and fire,” one resident told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity.The Saudi civil defence force sent air raid alerts overnight on Friday to residents of Riyadh, Jeddah and other cities including Yanbu, a major industrial port which is home to critical oil facilities. The military coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had destroyed a missile fired by the Yemeni group toward ​Riyadh.The all-clear was given shortly afterwards, but residents were encouraged not to gather in crowds.A Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the group had foiled unspecified “criminal attempts” ⁠in the Yemeni capital of Sana’a, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response. The group also said the Saudi air force had conducted hundreds of airstrikes against it in recent days.The UN security council condemned the continued ​Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia in a statement on Friday.

articles.title: Israeli president pardons combat medic who shot dead wounded Palestinian attacker
articles.excerpt: Israel’s president has pardoned a combat medic who shot dead a badly wounded Palestinian attacker who had stabbed a soldier in the occupied West Bank, in a case that divided the country a decade ago.Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter and his release after serving two-thirds of his 18-month sentence drew enormous attention in Israel, where military service is compulsory for most Jewish men.In his first interview after his release, Azaria said he would “act exactly the same, because that’s how I needed to act”.Azaria had approached Abdel Fattah al-Sharif as he lay on the ground, unarmed and badly hurt, after stabbing a soldier in the city of Hebron. A mobile phone video captured Azaria shooting al-Sharif in the head.The office of president Isaac Herzog said in a statement on Saturday that he acted on the recommendation of defence minister Israel Katz. The statement cited the time that had passed, and the spirit of the approaching Yom Kippur, or Day of Atonement, holiday as among the factors in the decision.Herzog’s office also said that Azaria, who was 20 when he was sentenced, had “expressed his sorrow” in his request. The statement noted that in an earlier request, he called his gunshot an “operational error”.In a separate statement, Katz called it a “right, humane and fitting decision” and said Azaria had been in a “complex operational mission”.But the military’s chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, had said in a letter to the defence minister that the pardon should not be granted, Israeli media reported.The conviction was a rare case of a military court ruling against a soldier for deadly action taken in the field. Top generals had pressed for his prosecution, while many in the Israeli public supported Azaria at a time when there had been a series of stabbings and car-ramming attacks by Palestinians or Israeli Arabs.

articles.title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary
articles.excerpt: First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as one and turned to applaud the film-makers for 25 minutes.The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.The film’s title comes from an Israeli military acronym used euphemistically to refer to the civilians expected to be killed in a military attack.Unfolding against the background of Tel Aviv at night, the participants – intelligence officers and other soldiers – describe a series of systems, some powered by AI, that select the thousands who should die in strikes, often at night and surrounded by their families.Perhaps most challenging for Israel’s political elite is that it is a story told exclusively in Hebrew by 24 anonymised Israeli military insiders, many of them from elite units.The documentary depicts a wide variety of viewpoints that all lead to the same conclusion: participation in a programme of mass killing where there were few boundaries between combatant and civilian, in a war where more than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed. Some describe being shamed by their experience. Some are neutral. Others describe excitement, and a sense of “fun” as they justify their actions.It will open in US cinemas from 30 September, with international distribution plans to be announced shortly. The ripples of ovation gathered in volume among the few who have seen the film before its New York premiere, but in Israel the film provoked a very different response.Rightwing political figures have rushed to accuse its directors – the Oscar-winning Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor – of “treason”.

articles.title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse
articles.excerpt: A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout.More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.Some Yemeni politicians are claiming that billions of dollars were offered to persuade the forces defending the west coast to abandon their position. It is thought as many as 30,000 well-equipped fighters retreated, raising questions about coordination, readiness and morale.The claim made by the governor of Hadramaut, one of Yemen’s largest governorates, did not identify the source of the payment, but others have tried to draw conclusions from the past links between the United Arab Emirates and the pro-government National Resistance Forces led by Tareq Saleh.

articles.title: Poison suspected in deaths of ten lions in game reserve in Tanzania
articles.excerpt: Investigation into 10 lion deaths in Tanzania focused on poisoning The lions were found dead inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a popular wildlife reserve in Tanzania. Deaths raise concerns over wildlife poisonings in East Africa. World September 20, 20265:39 PM ET Lions walk in the Ngorongoro Crater in Ngorongoro Conservation Area, west of Arusha, northern Tanzania, Monday, Jan. 19, 2015. Mosa'ab Elshamy/AP hide caption toggle caption Mosa'ab Elshamy/AP Ten lions found dead in a wildlife reserve in Tanzania are suspected to have been poisoned, according to wildlife officials. The animals were discovered on Friday in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, home to pastoral tribal communities that raise cattle. It is also one of the most visited tourist destinations in the country. "Preliminary findings suggest the animals may have died after ingesting poison," a statement from The Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority said, adding the authority has launched a full investigation "to determine the cause of the incident and identify those responsible." Large animals are under threat across East Africa, in places where they frequently come into conflict with humans. An investigation is underway in neighboring Kenya, where over the summer, 18 elephants died from suspected poisoning. Police have arrested four people. According to Kenya's Wildlife Service, preliminary tests showed the elephants may have ingested cyanide. Tomato farmers in the Amboseli region are known to use banned pesticides on their crops. But growers deny using cyanide. Tanzania is home to Africa's largest lion population, about half the world's wild lions. But they are listed as a vulnerable population by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Lions are under threat from shrinking habitat and poaching. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area in Tanzania is a UNESCO World Heritage Site protected under international law.
