articles.title: The pro-Israel censors are starting to lose
articles.excerpt: For decades, Israel’s greatest advantage in the West was not simply military or political support. It was narrative power.Israel and its supporters enjoyed enormous influence over the boundaries of acceptable discussion about Palestine: which violent incident received attention, whose security mattered the most, which historical context was relevant and, crucially, what criticism of Israel could be allowed in public.That power has not disappeared. But the extraordinary controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from Ed Sheeran’s US tour shows how rapidly it is eroding.The fact that the American rapper was dropped from the tour after he spoke about Palestine on stage meant that the old system worked. A powerful billionaire objected. Venues applied pressure. The artist disappeared from the stage.What was different this time was the backlash.In response to the censorship, every remaining support act on Sheeran’s tour walked away. Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga all withdrew. Meanwhile, ticket prices for Sheeran’s remaining concerts plunged, in some cases losing 50 percent of their value, as many fans felt outraged.Macklemore stood his ground and pledged the $1m he had earned from his appearances to six organisations supporting Palestinians. Subsequently, the media reported Sheeran would donate $2m towards humanitarian relief in the region.All of this has helped generate further donations and attention for Palestinian aid organisations, including a $1m pledge from children’s educator Ms Rachel.Consider what happened.An attempt to push “Free Palestine” off the stage resulted in Palestine receiving vastly more attention, artists abandoning one of the world’s biggest tours and more funds being donated to Palestinian organisations.The attempt to control the message amplified the message itself.

articles.title: India’s New Eye in the Sky: EOS-05 Satellite and What It Means for South Asia
articles.excerpt: The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) recently launched a new surveillance satellite designated as EOS-05 into geosynchronous earth orbit (GEO). The launch was carried out with the GSLV-F17 rocket. The satellite – launched on September 4 – is the first earth observation satellite deployed in GEO by India. The satellite will allow New Delhi to continuously observe the subcontinent from an altitude ranging between 34,903 km and 35,884 km. The chairman of ISRO, V. Narayanan, said that “EOS-05 will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from the geo orbit providing important strategic data for the country.” The launch of the satellite is part of India’s long-term plan to strengthen its intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities. The satellite will provide India with the capability to persistently track military movements in the subcontinent – especially Pakistan’s naval warships, aircraft, strategic assets movements, and force mobilization during crisis time. A new eye in the sky is an important military asset for India and can increase its counterforce capabilities in the age of emerging and disruptive technologies. India’s current space architecture consists of navigation, communication, ISR, and scientific satellites. For the purpose of communication, India has three dedicated military satellites – two of which are used by the Indian Navy and one by the Indian Air Force. Besides this, India has around 10 satellites that are dual-capable and can be used for military communication. The Indian navigation satellitessystem – known as Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) – has three operational satellites, IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I , and NVS-01. However, for basic positioning service four satellites are required in orbit ; the next satellite NVS-03 would be launched soon.

articles.title: Abroad, India’s RSS Speaks of ‘Love.’ At Home, Its Affiliates Attack Christians.
articles.excerpt: Sutahata is a rural place in the eastern Indian state of West Bengal, which has been ruled by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) since the May 2026 state elections. There, on August 26, about 50 people gathered at Goutam Bera’s residence in Ranichak village. It was a house fellowship gathering that involved Bible study and prayer. Many attendees were Hindus, mostly friends and acquaintances of the Bera family. The news of the gathering reached members of Hindu supremacist organizations. One of them broadcast a live video on Facebook while on his way to Bera’s place. They had heard a Christian priest had gone there to convert Hindus. “Let’s see what they are up to,” he said. By the time the livestreamer reached Bera’s house, some of his fellows were already there. They barged into the house, abused those present and threw people out, before allegedly manhandling the rest of the attendees. “You are Hindus. You have idols of Hindu deities at home. How could you bring in a Father and practice Christianity?” one can be heard shouting. “They have started this Jesus business now. See, we have recovered a Bible! My God, they have a Bible here!” One video shows the intruders – carrying saffron flags – ordering the prayer attendees, rather rudely and loudly, to chant “Hare Krishna, Hare Ram” and “Jai Shree Ram.” Another video shows the cops taking the prayer attendees to a police vehicle. At one point, people from the crowd can be heard shouting: “Thrash them, thrash them!” According to Joy Kumar Ghughu, the pastor who was reading from the Bible, the police first took 17 prayer attendees, including him, to the Sutahata block primary health center for treatment and a medical check-up. They were then taken to the Sutahata police station, where everyone was interrogated about the intention behind the gathering. Their mobile phones were examined. At about 8 p.m., they were told they could go.

articles.title: From Symbolism to Strategy: The Expanding Operational Role of Women in Baloch Militancy
articles.excerpt: On May 22, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), one of the principal armed groups in Pakistan’s Baloch insurgency, announced the formation of a dedicated women’s wing and named Shaynaz Baloch as its commander. The announcement was significant not simply because it placed a woman in a more visible position within the organization, but because it appeared to formalize a trend that has been developing since 2022: the expansion of women’s participation in Baloch militancy from largely symbolic and support roles into direct operational activity. The development raises a broader question: Why are Baloch militant organizations expanding women’s roles now, and what does this mean for an insurgency historically dominated by men? The shift can be traced most clearly to April 2022, when Shari Baloch carried out a suicide attack at the Confucius Institute at the University of Karachi, killing three Chinese teachers and their Pakistani driver. The BLA claimed responsibility and presented her as its first female suicide operative. Since then, several other women have been linked to suicide operations attributed to BLA factions. In June 2023, Sumaiya Qalandrani Baloch carried out a suicide attack targeting a military convoy in Turbat. In August 2024, a woman identified by the BLA as Mahal Baloch conducted a vehicle-borne attack against a Frontier Corps facility in Bela. In March 2025, Mahikhan Baloch carried out another suicide attack against a paramilitary convoy in Kalat. In November 2025, the trend extended to another major Baloch armed group, the Baloch Liberation Front (BLF), when Zareena Rafiq carried out a vehicle-borne attack against a Frontier Corps facility in Nokundi. The pattern suggests that the use of women is no longer confined to an isolated form of militant propaganda. It is becoming part of how some Baloch armed groups recruit, operate, and present themselves.

articles.title: Shipki La and the Battle Over the History of China-India Trade
articles.excerpt: After a six-year hiatus, the China-India border trade via Shipki Pass, a 3,930-meter pass in Himachal Pradesh’s Kinnaur district, resumed on August 1, 2026. After the 2020 Galwan military standoff, the border trade from this pass, often called the “Gateway to Tibet,” was suspended. With limited operations and economic scope but significant political symbolism, the resumption of border trade has also rejuvenated interest in the competing legitimacy narratives over the Tibet question. According to China’s state-affiliated think tanks and media, border trade via the Shipki L Pass dates to the 7th to 9th centuries when the Tubo Empire reigned over the plateau. China frames trade along this route as a sub-set of the Silk Road. Between the 14th and early 20th centuries, Chinese tellings claim Tibet as a commercial bridge between China and South Asia, while in the late 18th century, the Qing Dynasty of China took measures to standardize trade activities between Tibet and its neighboring countries, for “better management” of Tibet. As per the Chinese accounts, the “peaceful liberation” of Tibet in 1951 and the signing of the Panchsheel Pact led to the abolishment of India’s trade “privileges” in Tibet and the formalization of a new paradigm for Indo-Tibetan trade. China claims to have set Sino-Indian border trade free from unequal terms set by colonial rule, ushering in an era of normalized development. Cut to the present: the reopening of Shipki La Pass, despite the minuscule trade volume, is received by Chinese media as a welcome move toward improving China-India strategic ties. Every aspect of the Chinese reading of history sidelines the Tibetan side of the story. For starters, what the Chinese narrative misses is the independent agency Tibet exercised before 1951. By contrast, Tibetan scholars characterize Shipki Pass as a major route for trade and cultural exchange between Indian territories and Tibet, independent of Chinese involvement.

articles.title: Infrastructure Gaps Test Pakistan’s Flagship CPEC Industrial Zone, Field Survey Finds
articles.excerpt: FAISALABAD — Allama Iqbal Industrial City (AIIC), the first Special Economic Zone prioritized under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), has drawn more than 327 billion rupees ($1.2 billion) in committed investment and allotted 223 of 424 planned plots. But a field survey of the zone’s authority and four operating firms – including a China-Pakistan joint venture – found that basic infrastructure has not kept pace with that investment. The zone management itself now lists the resulting gaps among its most urgent priorities. The survey was conducted on-site using structured research instruments and covered Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development & Management Company (FIEDMC), which administers the 3,966-acre zone along the M-4 Motorway, and four operating firms; the findings are diagnostic rather than statistically representative. It found that water is supplied only through self-boring – individual firms drilling and managing their own wells – because no zone-wide piped potable network exists. Sewerage infrastructure remains under construction, while the zone’s assessment indicates that no Combined Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) has yet been funded, leaving firms to manage industrial wastewater largely on their own. “CETP and utility reliability” was the single most urgent reform named by FIEDMC’s own senior officials – spanning its general manager for engineering and its estate, zone, and land managers – when asked directly what the AIIC needs most. They also flagged the need to make the zone’s “One-Window Operation” facilitation service fully functional and time-bound, and to establish dedicated public transport and stronger security for workers commuting to the site. Those official priorities broadly align with concerns reported by the four tenant firms surveyed independently.

articles.title: The Nexperia Case Was Actually a Success. Does Europe Know That?
articles.excerpt: The July 2026 meeting between Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma and China’s Commerce Minister Wang Wentao was cordial. That might have come as a surprise given the tensions that erupted between China and the Netherlands following a high-profile dispute about Nexperia in the fall of 2025. The new Dutch government made it clear that it wanted to patch up ties with Beijing. Underneath the mess, the Nexperia incident was actually a comparatively successful economic security intervention – and that carries important lessons for Europe. At the July 2026 talks, the Chinese side called on the Dutch to “promote the proper resolution of disputes involving relevant companies,” a clear reference to the Nexperia case. Meanwhile The Hague is keen to let the courts move ahead. Nexperia’s Chinese owner, Wingtech, claims Nexperia China is now an independent producer, while Nexperia expects the worst shortages on the European side to ease by year’s end. China’s position of power means that a split of the company appears unavoidable, but at least its European business was saved. There remain many uncertain factors, not the least Wingtech’s arbitration procedure against the Dutch state incorrectly claiming expropriation while a court case that could permanently replace management is underway. Yet, a combination of not all Anglophone press fully grasping what really happened, Chinese distortion of the facts, and some Dutch ministerial amateurism raise the risk that Europeans draw the wrong conclusions about a vital policy area. Acting on the back-foot in response to a clear threat to European economic security, the Dutch economic affairs minister and Nexperia’s European leadership faced Beijing’s usual recipe of escalating to force the other to de-escalate when they moved to protect the automotive chip manufacturer. The minister’s moves should have been planned better, yet it was necessary to finally call a halt to the company’s hollowing out by its Chinese owners.

articles.title: Making the Most Out of Growing US-Uzbekistan Trade and Investment
articles.excerpt: The purchase of U.S.-made commercial aircraft and an Uzbek company’s historic opening of a manufacturing facility in Kentucky demonstrate the dynamic and growing economic relations between the United States and Uzbekistan. As U.S. diplomatic engagement with Tashkent increases – new contracts and trade and investment frameworks signed – understanding each country’s priorities and objectives will help explain this new chapter of the partnership. Moreover, stronger trade and investment numbers must translate into employment opportunities and an improved quality of life for the Uzbek population. Relations between Washington and Tashkent have generally strengthened over the past couple of years. U.S. President Donald Trump and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will next meet in December, as Trump has invited the Uzbek leader to be a guest at the G-20 summit in Miami. Stronger diplomatic links are translating into trade and investment deals. In June, the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) Ambassador Jamieson Greer visited Tashkent and signed “an early harvest of trade commitments to strengthen the bilateral economic and investment relationship.” Specifically, Tashkent committed “to eliminate or reduce tariffs” on U.S. industrial goods and agricultural products. In contrast, Washington committed “to provide favorable consideration” in tariff actions for Uzbekistan’s industrial goods and agricultural products. The two sides are also working to conclude an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and Investment. Also in June, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) launched the U.S.-Uzbekistan Joint Investment Platform, which will “aim to identify strategic investments in Uzbekistan for U.S.” in areas like energy, infrastructure, critical minerals, transportation and logistics infrastructure. The topic of investment in critical minerals, energy, and transportation was also reportedly discussed during a meeting between Mirziyoyev and Sergio Gor, the U.S.

articles.title: 4 Fault Lines that Could Shape the Trump-Xi Summit
articles.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet next week at the White House in Washington, D.C., provided that the “conditionalities” attached to the summit are met. This will be the second leaders’ summit between Trump and Xi this year, following the U.S. president’s visit to Beijing in May. This will be Xi’s first visit to the U.S. capital in a decade, after he met then-U.S. President Barack Obama in 2016. Back then, the agenda centered on the much-touted issues of cyberespionage and commercial hacking. Today, there are new concerns. Both domestically and internationally, this visit is taking place amid considerable friction. On the domestic front, the United States will be holding midterm elections roughly 40 days after the visit. This makes the timing an unusual choice, as noted by Pew Research: many Americans still view the Chinese leader unfavorably, despite a 6-percentage-point rise since last year. Presidents generally avoid such risks to optics as midterms near. At the international level, the world is still living under the shadow of the Iran-U.S. war. Consequently, Brent crude is trading around $100 per barrel. At the same time, the China-Russia alignment has deepened; a few months ago – just after the last Trump-Xi summit, in fact – Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed their close partnership and signed a joint statement to deepen their strategic partnership. Beijing is underwriting Moscow’s war machine in Ukraine as Washington prepares to welcome Xi. Meanwhile, Pew Research noted in another survey that Beijing is viewed favorably in more countries than Washington, adding another nuance to the global attention focused on the summit. However, one must note that Beijing has yet to officially confirm the meeting, even though the United States has given the date of September 24.

articles.title: Drones Offer Central Asia an Escape From Foreign Dependency
articles.excerpt: Drones are everywhere in the news and on the frontlines of the Iran-U.S. War and the Russia-Ukraine War, but their most recent use on a battlefield in Central Asia represents a long-term issue – continued dependency on foreign suppliers. The Central Asian states may just be replacing their long-term Russian security dependency with a Turkish one. Central Asian leaders risk deepening this dependency and worsening security vulnerabilities as they announce deals with foreign suppliers that are often headquartered in a single state – Turkiye. However, developments in 2026 show that opportunities for local development and production that would benefit regional economies without offloading security responsibilities exist. Local politicians just need to invest locally. In the 2022 border conflict between Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, Turkiye’s Baykar Bayraktar TB2 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) played a well-publicized role. After that conflict, Bishkek decided to deepen its Turkish dependency, ordering Aksungur and Akinci platforms, both from Turkish manufacturers, TAI and Baykar, respectively. It had already ordered additional TB2s and Anka (from TAI) as well. Drones are certainly cheaper than manned aircraft, but these imported platforms weren’t without cost. Civil servants took a pay hit to fund the purchase of the new systems. And this doesn’t factor in the cost of operations and maintenance. To keep these aircraft flying with spare parts, ammunition, and sensors will require continual funding. When buying any big-ticket item, that platform is committing the state to long-term sustainment with certain suppliers. Given Turkiye’s mercurial defense policy in recent years, can Bishkek rely on adequate sustainment in the event of another conflict? Turkiye, a NATO ally, hoped to procure F-35s, but acquired Russian S-400s, and is reportedly trying to resell those air defense system to the UAE, before aiming to rejoin F-35 talks.

articles.title: To Succeed in AI, South Korea Is Reinventing Its Developmental State Model
articles.excerpt: South Korea has embarked on an ambitious plan by launching the “AI for All” initiative, which aims to make artificial intelligence (AI) widely accessible to all its citizens. This initiative reflects a broader effort to integrate AI into almost every corner of Korean society. Rather than treating AI simply as another emerging technology, South Korea increasingly views it as a technology that will help realize its domestic economic development plans and geoeconomic objectives, retain its technological advantages in key strategic industries, and gain a strong foothold in emerging technologies amid intensifying technological competition. The South Korean government plans to provide AI learning opportunities to approximately 5.14 million people in 2026. To support this initiative, it is developing AI services based on South Korea’s sovereign AI models, including a general-purpose AI chatbot that citizens will be able to use without charges or usage limits. More importantly, Seoul’s long-term ambition is to move toward an environment in which its citizens can have access to their own AI agents. This plan can be understood as part of a broader trend among East Asian countries, particularly South Korea and China, toward emphasizing the rapid implementation and widespread application of AI. This approach reflects the distinction drawn by Kai-Fu Lee in his book “AI Superpowers: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order,” in which he contrasted China’s implementation-driven model with the innovation-first strategy associated with the United States. It also differs from the European approach, which places greater emphasis on AI governance, regulation, fundamental rights, and data privacy. In many parts of the world, especially in liberal democracies, AI remains a subject of debate over safety concerns. In South Korea and other East Asian countries, however, the debate is different: it focuses on how rapidly AI can be deployed.

articles.title: China Is Moving Toward a New Form of Coercion at Sea
articles.excerpt: Since Beijing announced special maritime operations on June 6, its forces have grown more assertive – pushing patrols into new waters, rotating formations to regularize presence, and deploying research vessels that can conduct military reconnaissance. This all points to a new form of coercion taking shape. On July 4, the Global Times – a mouthpiece for the Chinese Communist Party – declared that China’s maritime patrols had entered “a new phase,” defined by a move towards “a more systematic, institutionalized, and long-term framework” and away from “isolated military exercises or patrols.” Recent deployments bear this out. Between June 6 and June 10, China’s Ministry of Transport carried out its first special operation in waters east of Taiwan, halting commercial vessels and requesting information on their points of origin and destination. While China has announced mandatory inspections during past exercises, it has never successfully enforced them. This time was different. Chinese Coast Guard ships conducted inspections en masse through radio communications with all transiting commercial vessels. Even foreign commercial vessels – including three vessels from Singapore, Benin, and Liberia – reported receiving radio messages from Chinese authorities to comply with requests. According to Chinese state news agency Xinhua, across those four days, Chinese maritime authorities inspected 198 passing vessels, and even “rectified violations involving three ships.” The sheer quantity of reported inspections, followed by a public announcement of the results, demonstrates China’s ability to govern vessel traffic in Taiwan’s waters. Beijing uses that as grounds to assert jurisdiction over the island and to push the narrative that cross-strait dynamics are China’s internal affairs. These operations may be testing grounds for an eventual quarantine, where China selectively permits commercial vessels to enter or leave, exerting immense pressure on Taiwan’s supply lines.

articles.title: Where Does North Korea’s Nuclear Program Stand in 2026?
articles.excerpt: Nearly two decades after international inspectors were expelled from North Korea, satellite imagery and open-source analysis remain the only windows the outside world has into Pyongyang’s nuclear program. What that window shows in late 2026 is a program that is visibly expanding, on multiple fronts at once. On August 28, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) issued a report to its Board of Governors documenting the construction of a second uranium enrichment facility at North Korea’s main Yongbyon nuclear complex. The new facility could house up to 28 centrifuge cascades, alongside an already-operating expanded annex at the Kangson enrichment site. The agency identified the new two-story building by comparing satellite images taken during its construction with state media photographs of a June 2026 visit by Kim Jong Un, during which centrifuges and cascades resembling those at known enrichment sites were visible. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told the Board that the continued operation of the Kangson and Yongbyon facilities, together with the reported further expansion of weapons-grade nuclear material production, was “a cause for serious concern.” The IAEA has not had inspectors on the ground in North Korea since 2009 and now builds its assessments entirely from commercial satellite imagery and open-source material, including North Korean state media itself. The picture built up over 2026 by independent monitors is consistent with the IAEA’s findings. Analysts tracking Yongbyon have documented near-continuous water discharge from the 5-megawatt-electric (MWe) reactor, North Korea’s original plutonium producer, consistent with it running through what is now believed to be its seventh irradiation cycle since October 2024, alongside periodic steam activity at the Radiochemical Laboratory suggesting reprocessing campaigns.

articles.title: How Looming US Sanctions Test India
articles.excerpt: On September 16, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act with a 262 to 159 vote. The U.S. Senate had passed the legislation on August 7 with an overwhelming majority, which means that the bill now awaits only presidential approval. Named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine, who spearheaded negotiations on the bill with the White House, the bill effectively allows President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on exports to the U.S. from the top five purchasers of Russian oil or natural gas, making exceptions for countries that import less than 15 percent of their natural gas from Russia and are taking “significant” steps to reduce the imports. Additionally, the bill provides for a range of sanctions against Russian officials and Moscow’s shadow fleet of vessels. Following the bill’s passage, Senator Richard Blumenthal publicly remarked that China and India “better clean up” their “act” and buy oil and gas “somewhere else.” As of August 2026, India was the second largest buyer of Russian oil, behind only China, leaving the two Asian giants most exposed to potential U.S. tariffs. Between December 2022 and August 2026, China accounted for 50 percent of Russia’s total crude exports, while India accounted for 37 percent.

articles.title: Arrests and Court Appearances Heighten Political Tensions in the Philippines
articles.excerpt: Philippine politics was anything but dull in the past two weeks. During this time, an arrest warrant was issued against Vice President Sara Duterte, who immediately posted bail and called for the resignation of her erstwhile ally, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was arrested for plunder while recovering in a hospital before being transferred to a regular jail facility. And lastly, former President Rodrigo Duterte made his first trial in-court appearance after more than a year of being under the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC). These high-profile events will continue to unfold and affect not just the Marcos presidency but also the narratives of the 2028 elections. Sara Duterte’s arrest warrant was issued in relation to the grave threats complaint filed against her after she said in an online video in late 2024 that she hired someone to kill Marcos and his wife. She posted bail to avoid arrest and called out Marcos for being ungrateful and betraying those who voted for him. Duterte minced no words against Marcos in a speech delivered in front of her supporters outside a local court: “You’re a liar, abusive. He has no debt of gratitude to our people and everyone who went to the precincts to put him in power. He has no shame.” The case is distinct from the current impeachment trial against Duterte, although the first article presented by the prosecution also related to the threats made by the vice president against the First Family. After the drama surrounding Duterte’s posting of bail, an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Romualdez in connection with his role in the flood control kickback scandal. The arrest was cited by Palace supporters as proof that Marcos is seriously pursuing accountability, since Romualdez is his close ally and first cousin. Romualdez spent a few days in the hospital before being placed in a regular prison cell.

articles.title: Indian Navy Augments Its Submarine Rescue Capability
articles.excerpt: On August 31, India commissioned INS Nipun, the second dedicated Diving Support Vessel (DSV) that serves as the mothership for the two Deep Submergence Rescue Vehicles (DSRVs) in service. With this, the Indian Navy crossed a threshold in a critical operational capability – submarine rescue – that has a bearing not just for India but for the entire region. Submarines are some of the most complex machines in existence and their operation is highly specialized. Submarine rescue takes that to another level and is a forte of a very small group of countries. Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan’s remarks at the commissioning ceremony in Mumbai aptly encapsulate this. The Nipun significantly enhances the capacity to respond to a distressed submarine, whether of the Indian Navy or that of a partner navy, he said, adding that this capability would also enable India to support submarine rescue and emerge as the “preferred submarine rescue partner” in the region. The Indian Navy signed a deal worth 193 million British pounds (around $217 million) with U.K.-based James Fischer Defense in 2016 under which it procured two DSRVs, a Launch and Recovery System (LARS), and a LARS-integrated decompression chamber. They were operationalized at Mumbai on India’s western seaboard at the end of 2018 and at Visakhapatnam on the eastern seaboard in early 2019. Concurrently, in September 2018, the navy signed a deal with state-owned Hindustan Shipyard Limited, located at Visakhapatnam, for the construction of the two DSVs, with the first vessel to be delivered in 36 months. Until the DSVs were completed, INS Sabarmati of the Ship Building Corporation of India acted as the interim ship for both the vessels. This left a major operational void, as it meant more time, which is the most critical factor in the event of a submarine disaster in the ocean depths. The two vessels were launched into water in September 2022, and the first, INS Nistar, was commissioned on July 18, 2025.

articles.title: Indonesian Parliamentary Committee Debates Changes to Fiscal Deficit Limit
articles.excerpt: Indonesian lawmakers have begun debating potential changes to the country’s fiscal deficit ceiling, with several ‌lawmakers arguing yesterday that President Prabowo Subianto’s administration should have the right to exceed the current limit in order to fund its ambitious welfare policies. During a public hearing in Jakarta yesterday, the House of Representatives’ Commission XI debated a series of revisions of the State Finance Law. Passed in the wake of the Asian financial crisis of 1997-1998, the law sets a maximum budget deficit of 3 percent of gross domestic product and limits government debt to 60 percent of GDP. Mukhamad Misbakhun, chairman of the House of Representatives’ Commission XI, told the hearing that the deficit limit should not necessarily be treated as a rigid annual threshold if the government needs additional fiscal space to support economic growth. “Is 3% really ‘sacred’?” said Mukhamad, according to a report in the Jakarta Globe. Misbakhun, who is also a lawmaker of the Golkar Party, a member of Prabowo’s expansive coalition, proposed that the law be revised to establish clear conditions under which a larger deficit could be permitted, such as when tax revenue is weak, or state energy subsidies rise due to a spike in global energy prices – as happened in Indonesia after the outbreak of the U.S.-Israel-Iran war earlier this year. “We have the momentum to get out of the middle-income trap, ​take 233 million people out of middle income and head to high income,” Misbakhun said, according to Reuters. “That needs growth expansion. How ‌are ⁠we going to expand growth if we lock ourselves and always talk about 3 percent?” Mohamad Hekal, deputy head of the committee and a member of Prabowo’s party Gerindra, agreed that changes to the budget deficit ceiling should be discussed.

articles.title: Why Is Thailand Not Prosecuting Members of the Mauerberger Network?
articles.excerpt: On their Whale Hunting blog in August 2025, Tom Wright and Bradley Hope began exposing the vast financial network built by the Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and the South African Benjamin Mauerberger, known in Bangkok as Ben Smith. In May 2026, the U.S. House Select Committee on China published a bipartisan report, “Crime, Corruption, and Power.” The report claims that a “South African fixer” is alleged to have operated between Cambodia’s crime hubs, developers linked to the Chinese Communist Party, and Thailand’s elite economy, laundering enormous illicit proceeds into Thai markets. All three footnotes cite Wright and Jacob Sims, a visiting fellow at Harvard University who specializes in Southeast Asia’s scam economy. Thailand appears in that report twice. The first mention of the country is as a victim of the regional scam economy, with domestic losses put above 115 billion baht ($3.5 billion) a year, according to a 2025 estimate by Global Anti-Scam Alliance. The second is the market where many of the profits from Southeast Asian scam centers come to rest. By my own count, those proceeds sit in more than 20 listed and unlisted Thai companies, in holdings worth over 26 billion baht ($778 million). Thailand has become rather good at finding this money, but it has not begun to prosecute the people who helped to move and launder it. The revelations have implicated a sitting member of the government. Vorapak Tanyawong, a former president of Krungthai Bank, was appointed deputy finance minister on September 19 of last year. He resigned 33 days later, after Whale Hunting reported that he had once been listed as an adviser to Cambodia’s BIC Bank, whose chairman is Yim Leak, and alleged that his wife had received $3 million in cryptocurrency from a Chinese-Cambodian criminal network. Vorapak, who has not been charged with any offence, has denied all of it.

articles.title: Why Malaysia Won’t Extradite Dr. Zakir Naik to India
articles.excerpt: The biggest viral video of the recently concluded BRICS Summit in New Delhi was not of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi shaking hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping, but of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim singing a Hindi film song. At a gala dinner during the summit, Anwar spotted a pianist in the hotel lobby and started singing Kishore Kumar’s evergreen “Khwaab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat” from the 1965 Dev Anand film, “Teen Deviyan.” Indian movies are very popular in Malaysia, and Anwar must have grown up listening to Bollywood songs because he has sung this song many times on past visits to India. But once the music stopped, Anwar returned to serious business, and one issue he must have been aware that every Indian journalist would ask him about was the extradition of Islamic preacher Dr. Zakir Naik. Naik, who faces multiple criminal charges in India relating to hate speech, inciting terrorism, and money laundering, moved to Malaysia in 2016 and has remained there since. India formally sent an extradition request to Malaysia in January 2018. New Delhi has also sought an Interpol Red Notice for Naik’s arrest. Interpol declined India’s request citing that the request was premature because a formal charge sheet had not been filed at the time of the original application. Anwar handled the issue with due maturity, given that the extradition of Naik is a deeply sensitive domestic political issue. He confirmed that the matter had been discussed with Modi but avoided making any commitment on handing Naik over. Malaysia, he said, had to proceed cautiously and respect the rule of law and the importance of bilateral relations. India and Malaysia have an extradition treaty, signed in 2010, but Naik’s case is different. Malay Muslims constitute more than 70 percent of the country’s population, and no party can afford to offend them. And since arriving in Malaysia, Naik has become very popular among Malay Muslims.

articles.title: Former Philippine President Duterte Makes First In-person Appearance at ICC
articles.excerpt: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court (ICC) for the first time on Wednesday, ahead of his trial for atrocities committed during his violent “war on drugs” campaign. Duterte, 81, has been in the court’s custody since his arrest in the Philippines in March 2025. He faces three charges of crimes against humanity for extrajudicial killings carried out during the anti-drug campaign, a flagship policy of his administration between 2016 and 2022. For all of the pre-trial hearings so far, including his initial appearance in March 2025, Duterte has appeared via video link from the ICC’s detention unit. He appeared yesterday before the ICC’s Trial Chamber III, which held a third status conference to discuss how to manage the sprawling case against Duterte. The Inquirer.net reported that the case involves “hundreds of thousands of pages of documents, more than 1,000 audio and video files, and an estimated 193 hours of direct examination by prosecution witnesses.” During the proceedings, Duterte sat quietly sipping water and at one point stood and waved to family ​members in the public gallery, Reuters reported. However, the physical condition of the former president, who appeared thin and haggard, raised the question of whether he will live to see a verdict – and whether he is even fit to stand trial. Duterte’s attorneys claimed last year that he was in frail health and that his condition was deteriorating in the ICC’s detention unit. In one filing in June, they argued that the ex-president’s illness and “advanced age” created “compelling humanitarian grounds” for judges to grant his interim release.

articles.title: What’s Wrong With US Pacific Islands Policy?
articles.excerpt: There is currently an active debate about U.S. policy in the Pacific Islands. Some are saying the U.S. is AWOL in the region. Others have said this is one of the most active times for U.S. engagement, including the Heritage Foundation, which just published a detailed “policy inventory” of announced U.S. activities in the region. What do I think? Let me start in a Pacific Islands way, with a story. In May 2025, I took a China-donated cargo ship from Yap to Woleai atoll, in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM). Several hundred Micronesians (from babies to grandmothers), five Chinese construction workers, and I slept on the deck, used communal bathrooms, and ate the food we brought along for the days-long trip down the island chain. By the time I got back to Yap weeks later, I had lice, parasites, and a leg wound that took U.S. military-grade salve to heal. I also had friends for life. Onboard the China-donated ship that is the only regular transport along the Yap island chain. Families eat and sleep on deck for up to weeks at a time. Photo by Cleo Paskal. Why did I go? The U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) had announced around $2 billion in infrastructure investments on the main island of Yap State, an island also called Yap. Meanwhile, I had heard from Micronesian friends that the Chinese were working on something in Woleai, in a different part of Yap State. There was also a Dolly Parton angle – but that’s for later. People in DoD assured me (and their superiors) that everything was fine. Knowing how the U.S. government operates in other parts of the Pacific, I wondered if they had the full picture. So, I packed a bag full of tins of Chef Boyardee, bottles of water, and Dramamine and went to take a look. Soon after I arrived on Woleai, the president of FSM, Wesley Simina, arrived on his own boat. After the traditional beach greeting, he and his entourage disappeared on one of the island’s few pick-up trucks. His wife rode on the truck’s bed.

articles.title: After a Self-Immolation at the UN, Rethinking What Beijing Fears on Tibet
articles.excerpt: On July 2, Lobga Rangzen, a Tibetan man who had taken the word meaning “independence and freedom” as his name, set himself on fire outside the United Nations headquarters in New York. His act came one day after China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law took effect. In a video posted before his death, he denounced the law as an erasure of Tibetan identity and called on Tibetans-in-exile to take up their responsibility. He chose the spot deliberately, too. Tibetans have looked to the U.N. for redress since 1950, when Tibet’s appeal first went to the new global body. The General Assembly passed resolutions on Tibet in 1959, 1961, and 1965. The 1961 resolution explicitly invoked Tibetans’ right to self-determination. Yet after the People’s Republic took China’s U.N. seat in 1971, the issue vanished from the organization’s agenda. Rangzen’s self-immolation was an indictment of six decades of silence. For weeks after his death, Tibetan communities across the globe marched and demonstrated. CNN, Radio Free Asia, and others covered it; the U.N. secretary-general’s spokesperson offered condolences, and the U.S. State Department reaffirmed its support for Tibetans. Then, within days, the coverage vanished. No government went beyond boilerplate statements of sympathy. For decades, the Central Tibetan Administration’s envoys and Tibetan human rights organizations have worked in Geneva, Washington, and Brussels with extraordinary persistence, winning legislation like the Resolve Tibet Act. Beijing’s position has never varied: Tibet is an “inalienable part of China.” The one channel that did exist, nine rounds of talks with the Dalai Lama’s envoys between 2002 and 2010, produced nothing, and those talks have been moribund for over 15 years. The strategy of seeking international support to enact change in Tibet has run its course. The world has heard Tibetans cry out since 1959. Sympathy has calcified into routine: statements, condemnations, calls for dialogue.

articles.title: The Potential Mismatch Between Japan and the US on China
articles.excerpt: As the two most powerful countries in the world today, it is incredibly important that U.S. President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington on September 24. But before that, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae of Japan is hoping to gain a meeting with Trump during her own visit to the United States for the U.N. General Assembly. Both Trump and Takaichi are scheduled to address the General Debate in New York on September 22; as of September 17 “nothing has been decided” regarding a potential meeting, according to Takaichi. The China-U.S. summit will have broad implications across a variety of policy areas, and there is no shortage of things for Trump and Xi to talk about. But it will be especially important for Japan, given not just its alliance with the United States, but also its close geographic proximity to China. Takaichi thus hopes to meet with Trump and share Japan’s perspective on China, in order to make sure Japanese interests are considered by its foremost partner. For Japan, China is a significant threat to its national security that needs to be managed with help from the United States. The security environment in the Indo-Pacific region is under pressure as China continues developing its military capabilities. According to Japan’s defense white paper released last month, “China has been intensifying its activities in the region surrounding Japan [and] extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain.” There are numerous examples of China putting pressure on Japan’s national security and ability to respond. It has upped its coast guard patrols around the island of Taiwan, creating a situation that could threaten Japanese security in the event of a contingency. Japan had to deploy fighters after Chinese and Russian planes were detected in airspace close to the Miyako Strait by Okinawa in June.

articles.title: Will Taiwan Fight? We Need Better Evidence.
articles.excerpt: Simon Shuster’s recent article in The Atlantic, asking whether Taiwan might simply “give up” in the face of growing pressure from China, attracted considerable attention in Taiwan and among the broader community of China and Taiwan watchers. Some praised the piece for its candid analysis and for asking uncomfortable questions that are too often avoided in discussions about Taiwan’s security. Others were somewhat less impressed. The article quickly came under fire from Taiwanese and (mostly) Taiwan-based foreign analysts, who pointed to factual errors, questionable interpretations of domestic politics, and what they saw as a selective and misleading portrayal of Taiwanese society. Legislator Puma Shen, one of those interviewed for the article, issued a public statement accusing Shuster of taking his comments out of context. The Taipei Times devoted an editorial to rebutting the article, and even Taiwan’s National Security Council weighed in, with Secretary General Joseph Wu publicly rejecting its central premise. Essentially, there are rather good reasons to take these criticisms seriously. Some concern basic facts and context, which are obviously important when making such a sweeping argument about Taiwan. That said, the reaction also exposed another problem. A significant part of the response has questioned what a foreign journalist who spent limited time in Taiwan and has no evident prior expertise on Taiwan or the region can really know about Taiwanese society. Critics pointed to a lack of understanding of Taiwanese politics, insufficient engagement with Taiwanese voices and opinion polls showing considerable willingness to defend Taiwan, and Taiwan’s own experience – from democratization and the Sunflower Movement to its remarkable response to COVID-19 – as evidence of a society capable of mobilizing when necessary. As compelling as these arguments are, none of them give us a particularly convincing answer either.

articles.title: The Space Security Landscape Is Deteriorating Rapidly
articles.excerpt: There is little doubt that great power competition is ramping up. Now, another front has opened, with the United States announcing that it has deployed a space weapon. China, and subsequently Russia, had been pushing the limits in space, testing advanced technologies with possible offensive uses in outer space, including cyber weapons, ground-based lasers, and artificial robotic arms that could be used for repairing satellites but also have obvious military and intelligence uses. Now the U.S. has responded by joining the developing arms race, which is likely to spur further competition. The space arms race now appears to be fully underway. The acknowledgement of U.S. space weapons was made by U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink. He revealed that the U.S. Space Force has launched “space control weapons” into orbit. Delivering a keynote address at a recent Air and Space Forces Association (AFA) conference, Meink said that “the United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action.” Not surprisingly, he justified this step with reference to the threats from China and Russia, both of which “continue to demonstrate aggressive maneuvers and are developing – and demonstrating – space weapons of their own.” Meink is not the only U.S. official who has talked about these new space weapons. Addressing the “State of the Space Force” at the AFA conference, Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess made an unequivocal claim that the U.S. Space Force “uses active space-based weaponry to support United States national defense.” He noted the “increasingly contested” space domain where adversaries have technologies that are meant to disrupt or destroy satellites in orbit. He also made a mention of hypersonic weapons that pose a threat to the United States and its allies and partners.

articles.title: China Is Building a Global Infrastructure for Its Cultural Industries
articles.excerpt: On September 4, Lingang New Area in Shanghai launched an AI+micro-drama overseas service station, with initial service points in Saudi Arabia, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland. The initiative is designed to help Chinese companies navigate overseas regulations, localize content, and connect production with distribution in foreign markets. The service station covers the full export chain including content development, production, translation, and distribution. Rather than simply helping companies sell finished dramas abroad, it brings several stages of the export process into one system. Online literature, games, and micro-dramas are increasingly described in China as the “New Three” of cultural exports. All three can be adapted, translated, and distributed through digital platforms, making the process of taking them overseas simpler. In July, Guangxi Publishing & Media Group launched FLYTOTO, an AI-powered platform for short-drama co-creation. The platform connects Chinese production teams and creators with audiovisual institutions in Southeast Asia. FLYTOTO offers tools for script analysis, automated video production, and multilingual translation, alongside computing and distribution support. The platform was launched alongside the 2026 China-ASEAN Micro-Drama Competition, which includes both live-action and AI-generated micro-dramas. For China, the cultural industry is moving beyond the export of finished content to the systems that allow content to be produced, adapted, and distributed across markets. This shift did not begin with AI micro-dramas, although they provide the latest examples. China Literature, one of China’s largest online publishing companies, launched its international Webnovel platform in 2017, initially bringing Chinese online fiction to readers abroad through translated works. Webnovel has since expanded beyond translation.

articles.title: BRICS Declaration: India’s Great U-turn on Iran
articles.excerpt: The Pulse | Diplomacy | South Asia The declaration endorsed most of Iran’s main diplomatic concerns without speaking a single word against its drone and missile attacks on its neighboring Gulf states. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian being honored at a meeting with a group of Indian religious leaders, intellectuals, and businesspeople in New Delhi, India, on Sept. 11, 2026, the eve of the 18th BRICS Summit. Credit: X/Iran in India Before the BRICS summit in New Delhi, political analysts had warned that India would have to do a very difficult tightrope walk given the presence of China, Russia, and Iran. It was a foregone conclusion that they would use this platform for U.S. bashing. With India’s current tug-of-war with the Donald Trump administration, the honchos at South Block (India’s foreign ministry headquarters) used nuanced vocabulary and calibrated the final declaration in such a way that the United States was not named, but the declaration explicitly called for an end to unilateral economic sanctions, protectionist trade measures, and arbitrary tariffs. The surprising outcome of the summit is this: what is being hailed as a triumph of strategic autonomy saw the dilution of India’s foreign policy since the advent of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The BRICS summit was billed as the Modi show, but Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stole that thunder if one looks at the details of the Delhi declaration. The declaration endorsed most of Iran’s main diplomatic concerns without speaking a single word against its drone and missile attacks on its neighboring Gulf states. There was likewise no mention of Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi rebels, who have in recent times increased attacks on Saudi Arabia and held sea trade across the Red Sea hostage.

articles.title: US Congressmen Call for Tougher Actions Against Key Southeast Asian Scam Enablers
articles.excerpt: Two leading U.S. congressmen have called on the Trump administration to undertake further investigations into Southeast Asia’s scam industry, claiming that government-led crackdowns are leaving many important enablers untouched. The request was conveyed in a letter by Brian Mast (R-FL), chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and John Moolenaar (R-MI), chairman of the Select Committee on China, dated Tuesday. In the letter, which was addressed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, the pair requested further actions to combat scam operations in Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar. In particular, Mast and Moolenaar requested a probe of 28 individuals and entities who have been accused of involvement in online scamming operations in the three nations, asking for a determination within 180 days as to whether they “meet the statutory criteria for imposition of sanctions” under U.S. law. The list includes businesspeople and government officials, including two sitting Cambodian ministers. “Americans are being scammed online at enormous and still growing rates, due primarily to a network of Chinese transnational criminal organizations based in Southeast Asia,” the two congressmen wrote. “These sanctions investigations would significantly degrade the financial, business, and political structures in Southeast Asia complicit in online scams that have scammed Americans out of tens of billions of dollars annually.” Online scamming operations have proliferated across mainland Southeast Asia since the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in loosely regulated parts of Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar. Coordinated predominantly by Chinese organized crime syndicates, these industrial-scale scam operations run romance-investment and crypto scams that target victims across the globe.

articles.title: Indian, Pakistani Naval Vessels Collide in Arabian Sea, Prompting Diplomatic Tensions
articles.excerpt: On September 15, PNS Hunain, a Pakistan Navy corvette, collided with an Indian Navy warship, INS Kolkata, in the north Arabian Sea, 220 kilometers east of Oman. The following day, India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) summoned Pakistan’s top-most diplomat in New Delhi, Chargé d’Affaires Saad Ahmad Warraich, to the foreign ministry to protest the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of ​Pakistani naval units. “While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement. Article 10 of the 1991 Agreement, which Pakistan reportedly flouted, states that naval ships and submarines belonging to the two countries should not come within three nautical miles of each other while operating in international waters. The agreement was signed as a confidence-building measure to put in place mechanisms for India and Pakistan to inform each other about military exercises or troop movements to prevent a crisis from arising due to the misreading of the other side’s intentions. It came following heightened tension when India conducted Brass Tacks, a massive military exercise in the states of Punjab and Rajasthan along the India-Pakistan border, in January 1987. Meanwhile, across the border in Pakistan, the response mirrored that of India, with Islamabad blaming India for the incident. “While the Pakistan Navy was undertaking its biennial exercise, SEASPARK-26, the Indian vessel carried out aggressive maneuvers in dangerously close proximity to a Pakistani naval ship, resulting in contact between the two vessels, ” the Pakistan Foreign Office said in a statement.

articles.title: Who Is to Blame for the Massive Death Toll in the Nepal Floods?
articles.excerpt: When a massive flood hit Nepal on August 26, Nepali social media split almost immediately into two camps of grief and anger. One camp blamed the government of China, saying hundreds of Nepalis – over 1,400 as of the last count – died because the warning had simply failed. Commentators accused China of sitting on satellite and disaster monitoring data that could have bought Nepal precious minutes of warning. A second, more painful narrative came from survivors and local officials themselves: yes, the word had reached them that flood was coming down. There simply wasn’t enough time to react before the disaster arrived. China’s embassy in Kathmandu called the claims that it had withheld information “completely false and misleading,” insisting Beijing shared information with the Nepali side in time. But the strongest pushback on the blame narrative didn’t come from Beijing at all, but from Nepal’s own disaster authority, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA). “There have been several discussions. Actually, Chinese approached the Nepal government several times,” NDRRMA director Dr Prakash Pokhrel told me. “The Nepali side needs to be more proactive to finalize the data sharing agreement.” In other words, the problem wasn’t China refusing to share data. It was Nepal not following through. Days after the flood, researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment published a technical reconstruction of the disaster. They found that a glacier in Langtang Lirung’s south slope, at roughly 5,200 meters in elevation, had fractured at 10:52 a.m. China time (8:47 a.m. in Nepal), sending an ice-rock avalanche that scoured downhill and grew into a debris flow. It covered 22 kilometers and reached Gyirong Port on the Chinese side of the border in about seven minutes, an average speed of nearly 50 meters a second.

articles.title: Malaysian PM Offers to Host Myanmar’s President in Refugee Repatriation Push
articles.excerpt: Malaysia is set to welcome Myanmar’s military-appointed president for an official visit, in a bid to expedite the return of thousands of Rohingya Muslim refugees. Speaking on a podcast yesterday, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said that he had invited Min Aung Hlaing to the country, on the condition that Myanmar agrees to take back citizens currently in Malaysia. “I invited him to say we can be friends, ​we can trade, we can accept Myanmar, but Myanmar must accept them [the refugees] back,” Reuters reported. If the trip eventuates, Malaysia will become the fifth member state of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to host Min Aung Hlaing since he took office in April, after trips to Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam. It will also become the first nation from maritime Southeast Asia to take such a step. The six maritime ASEAN states – Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Brunei, and Timor-Leste – have generally been more critical of Myanmar’s military than the nations of the mainland, since the coup of 2021. Malaysia in particular has been one of the most outspoken, repeatedly expressing frustration at the Myanmar military’s refusal to cease hostilities and counseling a harder ASEAN line. Anwar said yesterday that Malaysia was not ready to recognize Myanmar’s new government, ⁠but needed an authority to negotiate with on returning refugees. “To me, that’s better diplomacy than just shouting angrily at Myanmar. Who’s going to take them? Where do we ‌send ‌them? They don’t even have Myanmar citizenship,” he said. “We, following ASEAN, don’t want direct relations with Myanmar. So who are we ‌supposed to negotiate with?” While Malaysia’s hard line on Myanmar has softened somewhat over the past year, Anwar is under pressure to respond to the growing public hostility toward the Rohingya in Malaysia.

articles.title: Texas: ICE-Agent verletzt Mann bei Schüssen in liberaler Enklave Austin
articles.excerpt: Die genauen Umstände sind noch unklar. Lokale Medien berichten, dass das Opfer durch einen Schuss in den Torso verwundet und in ernstem, aber stabilem Zustand ins Krankenhaus gebracht worden sei.Laut der Polizeichefin von Austin, Lisa Davis, ereignete sich der Vorfall bei einem Verkehrsstopp am Sonntag ohne Beteiligung der örtlichen Polizei. Aufnahmen zeigen einen blauen Toyota unter einer Brücke, offenbar mit Einschüssen in der Tür. Weder der Name des Opfers noch der des Schützen sind bisher öffentlich. Das Heimatschutzministerium, das die Aktionen von ICE koordiniert, äußerte sich nicht. Bürgermeister: Unklar, wo sich der ICE-Schütze aufhältEin Problem: Laut Austins demokratischem Bürgermeister Kirk Watson wissen die Behörden in der Stadt nicht, wo sich der ICE-Schütze aufhält. »Meine Hoffnung ist, dass er die Stadt nicht verlassen hat. Vom Bundesstaat ganz schweigen.« Er erwarte, dass die Polizei von Austin und die Texas Ranger an den Ermittlungen beteiligt werden, so Watson. Die Stimmung in Austin ist aufgeladen. Am Tatort hatten sich am Sonntag Hunderte Demonstranten versammelt, die Polizei war teils mit Schutzschilden ausgerüstet.
articles.summary: 确切情况仍不清楚。当地媒体报道称，受害者躯干中弹受伤，被送往医院时情况严重但稳定。据奥斯汀警察局长丽莎·戴维斯称，该事件发生于周日一次交通拦截中，当地警方并未参与。录像显示一座桥下有一辆蓝色丰田汽车，车门上显然有弹孔。受害者姓名和开枪者姓名迄今均未公开。协调ICE行动的国土安全部未作表态。市长：不清楚ICE枪手身在何处。一个问题：据奥斯汀民主党市长柯克·沃森称，该市当局不知道ICE枪手身在何处。「我希望他没有离开这座城市。更不用说离开本州了。」沃森说，他期待奥斯汀警方和得克萨斯游骑兵参与调查。奥斯汀的气氛十分紧张。周日，数百名示威者聚集在案发现场，警方部分人员配备了防暴盾牌。

articles.title: Ergebnis der Mecklenburg-Vorpommern-Wahl: AfD siegt vor SPD, CDU fliegt aus Landtag
articles.excerpt: Die AfD hat nach offiziellen Angaben mit 38,2 Prozent der Stimmen die Landtagswahl in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern gewonnen. Das erklärte die Landeswahlleitung. Auf Platz zwei folgt die SPD mit 35,5 Prozent, zudem ziehen die Linke (6,5 Prozent) und die Grünen (5,7 Prozent) in den Landtag ein. Die CDU (4,9 Prozent) sowie das BSW (4,8 Prozent) scheitern knapp. Die AfD kommt demnach im neuen Parlament auf 32 Sitze, die SPD auf 29, die Linke wie die Grünen auf 5 Sitze.Erstmals wird die AfD damit stärkste Fraktion im Landtag von Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Gegenüber der Wahl von vor fünf Jahren haben die Rechtspopulisten ihr Ergebnis mehr als verdoppelt (damals 16,7). Der Kandidat der AfD für das Amt des Ministerpräsidenten, Leif-Erik Holm, leitete daraus einen Regierungsauftrag für seine Partei ab. Er werde mit den anderen Parteien über die Möglichkeit einer Zusammenarbeit sprechen. Allerdings haben bis auf das BSW bisher alle anderen politischen Kräfte eine Kooperation mit der AfD ausgeschlossen – und das BSW schaffte es am Ende nicht in den Landtag.Die SPD erlitt leichte Verluste (2021: 39,6 Prozent). Angesichts des Bundestrends zeigte sich die Partei mit dem Ergebnis dennoch zufrieden. »Was für eine Aufholjagd«, sagte Ministerpräsidentin Manuela Schwesig kurz nach Bekanntwerden der ersten Prognosen. In Umfragen vor der Wahl hatte die SPD lange deutlich unter 30 Prozent gelegen. Warum für viele Genossen nun trotzdem die Enttäuschung überwiegt, erfahren Sie hier .
articles.summary: 根据官方公布的数据，德国选择党（AfD）以38.2%的得票率赢得梅克伦堡-前波美拉尼亚州州议会选举。该州选举管理机构宣布了这一结果。社会民主党（SPD）以35.5%位居第二，左翼党（6.5%）和绿党（5.7%）也进入州议会。基民盟（CDU，4.9%）和莎拉·瓦根克内希特联盟（BSW，4.8%）则惜败，未能跨过进入议会的门槛。据此，AfD在新一届议会中拥有32个席位，SPD获29席，左翼党和绿党各获5席。这是AfD首次成为梅克伦堡-前波美拉尼亚州议会中最大的党团。与五年前的选举相比，这个右翼民粹政党的得票率增加了一倍多（当时为16.7%）。AfD的州长候选人莱夫-埃里克·霍尔姆由此为其政党提出了执政授权。他表示将与其他政党讨论合作的可能性。然而除BSW外，此前所有其他政治力量都排除了与AfD合作的可能——而BSW最终未能进入州议会。SPD遭受轻微损失（2021年为39.6%）。鉴于全国趋势，该党仍对结果表示满意。州长曼努埃拉·施韦西希在首批预测结果公布后不久表示：「这是一场多么惊人的追赶！」选前民调中，SPD长期明显低于30%。至于为何许多党内同志仍感到失望，可在此处了解。

articles.title: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität in München: Hacker erbeutet Daten von Studierenden
articles.excerpt: Ein unbekannter Hacker hat sich Zugang zu persönlichen Daten von Studierenden der Ludwigs-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in München verschafft. Der Angreifer habe ein IT-System der Hochschule mit Stammdaten zu Immatrikulationen geknackt, teilte die LMU mit. Der Hacker könne die Namen der Studenten und Studentinnen sowie Post- und E-Mail-Adressen, Geburtsorte, Bankdaten sowie weitere private Angaben beispielsweise zu früheren Bildungsabschlüssen erbeutet haben. Genaue Angaben dazu, wie viele Menschen betroffen sein könnten, machte die Hochschule nicht. Ebenso blieb unklar, ob nur die aktuellen Studierenden betroffen sind oder eventuell auch ehemalige.Nach Angaben der Universität waren im vergangenen Wintersemester 2025/26 mehr als 52.000 Studierende eingeschrieben. Die LMU gehört zu den größten Universitäten Deutschlands.Die Uni versicherte den Betroffenen, dass ihnen keine Nachteile für das Studium entstünden. Die Studierenden sollten nun allerdings besonders aufmerksam sein, insbesondere bei Kontaktversuchen. Den Hackerangriff auf die Universität bezeichnete von Brunn als schockierend, denn an der Hochschule sei eine »hohe IT-Kompetenz vorhanden«. Der Politiker kritisierte, es sei auch noch offen, wann der unbefugte Zugriff auf die Daten begonnen habe und wie lange er gelaufen sei. »Ursachen, Hergang und Verantwortlichkeiten müssen jetzt auf den Tisch«, sagte er.

articles.title: Bundesliga: SC Paderborn feiert gegen TSG Hoffenheim ersten Erstliga-Sieg seit mehr als sechs Jahren
articles.excerpt: Paderborns Trainer Ralf Kettemann hatte trotz des 0:3 bei Borussia Dortmund in der Vorwoche keine Änderungen in der Startformation vorgenommen. Auch das in dieser Saison in den ersten drei Spielen noch torlose Sturmduo Marvin Pieringer und Marino bekam eine weitere Chance.Und Marino hatte nach 13 Minuten die erste gute Gelegenheit für die Gastgeber, scheiterte mit seinem Schuss aber an Hoffenheims Torwart Oliver Baumann. Der TSG-Torhüter hatte nach dem schwachen Auftritt auf Kreta mit seiner Abrechnung mit Ex-Bundestrainer Julian Nagelsmann für Schlagzeilen gesorgt. In Paderborn trat Baumann gewohnt souverän auf. Allerdings war auch Baumann beim Paderborner Führungstreffer machtlos. Nach einer abgewehrten Ecke fiel Castaneda der Ball vor die Füße, der Schuss des Mittelfeldspielers wurde unhaltbar für Baumann abgefälscht. Der Jubel auf Paderborner Seite war groß. Erstmals in dieser Saison lief die Kult-Torhymne «Hermann Löns, die Heide brennt» in der Arena.Kurz zuvor hatten die Ostwestfalen noch großes Glück gehabt, dass ein Schuss von Hoffenheims Vladimir Coufal an den Pfosten geprallt war. Ansonsten enttäuschten die Hoffenheimer aber weitgehend. Wie schon auf Kreta konnten die Kraichgauer mit dem vielen Ballbesitz nichts anfangen. Paderborn hatte so wenig Mühe, die Führung zu verteidigen und kurz vor der Pause sogar noch auszubauen. Marino verwandelte ein schönes Zuspiel von Laurin Curda zum 2:0.

articles.title: Wolodymyr Selenskyj kündigt Treffen mit Donald Trump in New York an
articles.excerpt: Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj hat in der nächsten Woche ein Treffen mit US-Präsident Donald Trump angekündigt. Demnach telefonierte Selenskyj mit Trump und besprach mit ihm eine Reihe von Themen, wie er auf Telegram mitteilte. Ein Treffen in New York, wo beide Präsidenten an der Generalversammlung der Vereinten Nationen teilnehmen, könne mit Blick auf mögliche neue Verhandlungen zur Beendigung des Ukrainekriegs viel bewirken. »Die diplomatische Dynamik ist da«, sagte er. Ein genaues Datum für das Treffen nannte Selenskyj zunächst nicht.»Der Friedensprozess hat höchste Priorität«, sagte Selenskyj nach dem jüngsten Besuch von US-Chefunterhändler Steve Witkoff und Trumps Schwiegersohn Jared Kushner in Kyjiw. Die beiden hatten das erste Mal überhaupt in ihrer Vermittlerrolle die Ukraine besucht und sich über die Lage in dem Land informiert. Zuvor waren sie zum wiederholten Mal in Russland gewesen, das seit mehr als viereinhalb Jahren Krieg gegen die Ukraine führt. Selenskyj: »Bereit zu ernsthaften Schritten«Geplant ist demnach, die direkten Verhandlungen zwischen Kyjiw und Moskau unter US-Vermittlung über ein Ende des Kriegs wiederaufzunehmen. Russland hält das im Oktober für möglich. Im vergangenen Winter waren die Gespräche in die Sackgasse geraten und schließlich wegen des Irankriegs abgebrochen worden. Witkoff und Kushner, die im Nahen Osten ebenfalls vermittelten, unternehmen nun einen neuen Anlauf. »Es gibt Ideen zu Deeskalationsmaßnahmen und grundlegenden Sicherheitsfragen«, sagte Selenskyj. »Wir arbeiten gemeinsam mit dem amerikanischen Team und sind bereit, wirklich ernsthafte Schritte zu unternehmen.« Details nannte er nicht. Der Präsident hatte zuletzt von den USA immer wieder vor allem Flugabwehrraketen gefordert, um sich gegen die russischen Angriffe mit ballistischen Raketen zu verteidigen.

articles.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Wie Menschen auf den AfD-Erfolg reagieren
articles.excerpt: Luana Partimo, SPIEGEL:»Mecklenburg-Vorpommern hat den Landtag gewählt. Wir sind heute in Schwerin unterwegs und haben die Leute gefragt, was sie von dem vorläufigen Ergebnis halten.«Passant:»Blamabel. AfD, stärkste Kraft, ist schon ein starkes Stück.«Passant:»Mich lässt das ein bisschen kalt, tatsächlich, einfach aus dem Hintergrund, weil es irgendwie zu erwarten war.«Luana Partimo, SPIEGEL:»Hatten Sie gehofft, dass es anders kommt?«Passantin:»Ja, definitiv. Ich hatte gehofft, dass die SPD auf jeden Fall einen großen Rutsch hat, nach oben, auch die Grünen.«Luana Partimo, SPIEGEL:»Was macht das mit Ihnen?«Passant:»Mir macht es keine Angst mehr, auf mich bezogen. Mir macht es Angst, wenn ich an meine Kinder und die Enkel denke.«Passantin:»Ich bin in der ehemaligen DDR noch geboren und man hatte so eine kritische Herangehensweise und auch ein kritisches Hinterfragen der Sachen. Und das finde ich ganz, ganz schlimm, dass das verloren gegangen ist.«Luana Partimo, SPIEGEL:»Was glauben Sie: Warum ist die AfD hier stärkste Kraft geworden?«Passant:»Ich weiß nicht. Vielleicht Enttäuschung von den etablierten Parteien?«Passant:»Ich denke mal, es ist wirklich der Frust der Zeiten davor von den ganzen Regierungen davor, was passiert ist. Und es ist aber auch sehr viel Propaganda dabei, sage ich. Also, das hat die AfD leider gut gemacht. Gerade was die Ausländerkriminalität angeht, wenn Sie das immer sehr oft erwähnen mit: Die sind so schlimm und hier und da. Aber wenn man sich die Statistiken anschaut, ist ja immer ganz anders.«Luana Partimo, SPIEGEL:»Was sagen Sie? Wie soll es jetzt weitergehen?«Passant:»Junge Frau, wenn ich das wüsste, würde ich nicht hier stehen. Dann würde ich da oben sitzen und sagen, wo es langgeht.«

articles.title: Russland: Prognosen sehen Kremlpartei Einiges Russland als Sieger bei Parlamentswahl
articles.excerpt: Die Kremlpartei Einiges Russland ist bei der dreitägigen Parlamentswahl erwartungsgemäß zur Siegerin erklärt worden. Die seit gut 20 Jahren regierende Partei kam nach dem Ausschluss der Antikriegspartei Jabloko laut Wahlnachbefragungen auf 49,4 Prozent der Stimmen. Die Wahlen in Russland gelten wegen des Ausschlusses einer echten Opposition und wegen fehlender unabhängiger Berichterstattung in den Medien als weder fair noch frei.Laut den Prognosen schafften auch die Kommunistische Partei (14,2 Prozent), die ultranationalistische Partei LDPR (10,7) und die vergleichsweise neue, für ein liberales Großstadtpublikum gegründete Partei Nowyje Ljudi (9,7) sowie die Partei Gerechtes Russland (6,6) wieder den Einzug in die Duma. Es handelt sich nicht um Ergebnisse, sondern um Angaben von Wählern nach Abgabe ihrer Stimmen. Alle Parteien sind kremltreu und unterstützen den russischen Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine. Die Wahl gilt als wichtige Bestätigung für den Kriegskurs von Kremlchef Wladimir Putin. Für die Partei Einiges Russland kandidierten Dutzende Kriegsveteranen. Die seit über 20 Jahren regierende Kremlpartei war wegen einer massiven Wirtschaftskrise, Kriegsmüdigkeit und Unzufriedenheit der Menschen mit einem schwierigen Wahlkampf konfrontiert.Kritik an WahlrechtsverstößenEs war auch die erste Abstimmung in dem Land seit Beginn von Putins Krieg gegen die Ukraine im Februar 2022. Der russische Präsident hatte die Menschen aufgefordert, mit ihrer Stimme einen Betrag zum Sieg zu leisten. Die Wahlbeteiligung lag nach amtlichen Angaben mit mehr als 56 Prozent höher als 2021. Überprüfbar sind die Angaben der vom Kreml gesteuerten Wahlkommission nicht. Gegen den Protest der Ukraine wurde die Wahl erstmals auch in den von Russland kontrollierten Teilen der annektierten ukrainischen Regionen Luhansk, Donezk, Saporischschja und Cherson abgehalten.

articles.excerpt: Issa Remmo, der als Oberhaupt des Berliner Remmo-Clans gilt, hat nach Berichten der »Berliner Morgenpost« die Wahlparty des Neuköllner Bezirksverbands der Linken besucht. Auch »Bild«-Reporter berichten über den Besuch. (Alles Wichtige zu den Landtagswahlen hier live .) Er würde »keinen judenfeindlichen Politiker wählen«.Die Linke in Berlin-Neukölln betonte, dass es weder politische noch persönliche Beziehungen zu Remmo gebe. »Es handelte sich um eine öffentliche Veranstaltung, zu der auch ungeladene Personen Zutritt hatten«, teilte Jorinde Schulz aus dem Bezirksvorstand der Neuköllner Linken mit. »Uns war die Person und ihre Anwesenheit im Speziellen nicht bekannt, sie steht nicht auf unserer Anmeldeliste. Es gibt weder politische noch persönliche Beziehungen zu dieser Person.« Der Besuch der Wahlparty habe daran »selbstverständlich nichts geändert«.
